key_terms.هَوَى النَّفْسِ: appetite of the soul / lower self

ai.seo_question: Why is obedience to God often difficult while disobedience feels pleasurable?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates a fundamental psychological principle of spiritual struggle (jihad al-nafs), noting that divine obedience often requires overcoming initial aversion, whereas sin appeals to base desires. This insight underscores the Shia emphasis on conscious self-discipline (muraqabah) to align the restless soul (nafs) with divine will, transforming natural inclinations into conscious acts of worship. The exhortation to 'subdue the self' reflects the broader ethical framework where victory over one's ego is considered a prerequisite for spiritual proximity to God.

en.sayed-ali-raza: every obedience to Allāh is unpleasant in appearance while every disobedience to Allāh has the appearance of enjoyment. Allāh may have mercy on the person who kept aloof from his desire and uprooted the appetite of his heart, because this heart has far-reaching aims and it goes on pursuing disobedience through desires.
